personas.why: I stay to see what overrides the wrong STOP. Seeing it change to CHECK FOOTAGE makes the diagram worth saving.
One flag in 23 gets my attention. I want to see which rep earned it, not read the boxes that lead to the judge.
I can already picture the friend I'd send the swinging clip to. The countdown feels like the start of a different reel.
I stay to find out what went wrong. Once I see the legs swinging, I think I've got the answer and scroll.
I can follow the real knee making a wave. When the footage gives way to a flowchart, I lose the comparison I wanted to see.
The skeleton locking on and the counter ticking up make this feel buildable. I'd send it to a project partner and comment FORM for the diagram.
Comparing against his own best is interesting, and the false alarm tests that idea. Once the verdict changes to CHECK FOOTAGE, the next exception feels like extra detail.
The false alarm earns my attention. Two judges agreeing on footage from the same angle doesn't tell me the remaining STOP was right.
I like that the diagram answers a specific question: what happens when the numbers and the video disagree? I'd save the final frame.
The turn towards the camera explains the mistake in two seconds. I've got a useful filming tip; the model names and per-set cost are where I leave.
The ghost overlay stops my thumb, but three ticks to announce a tool I've already seen in action spend that attention without giving me anything new.
I remember the green ghost over the swinging legs. When we're suddenly tracing a lunge, I'm no longer sure which set I'm meant to care about.
The interesting part is that the system can decline to give a verdict. I'd comment FORM to see how that decision is implemented.
The camera turn is a convincing failure case. I'd watch through and ask how often both agents agree on the wrong answer.
I'd replay the raw swing and the turned lunge to show a client what a camera can miss. Shorter range alone doesn't sell me on 'never have done.'
I get the gym-buddy joke from the actual rep. I'd rather see another example than wait for WORKOUT ANALYSER ONLINE.
